To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
magnetic resonance imaging accurately demonstrated the presence and extent (cephalad and caudal) of vena caval thrombosis in 20 patients with a variety of primary tumor histologies.

magnetic resonance imaging accurately demonstrates vena caval tumor invasion by renal cell carcinoma and that it is superior to venacavography or computerized tomography in demonstrating the cephalad extension of the tumor thrombus.
MRI accurately delineated the vena caval tumor extent and avoided the need for an inferior venacavogram.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the magnetic resonance imaging for the assessment of vena cava tumor thrombi.
the development of a new approach to magnetic resonance imaging in patients with vena cava tumor thrombi.
the development of an efficient method to detect and locate the presence of thrombi in a blood vessel.

magnetic resonance imaging is the best noninvasive imaging technique for the assessment of renal cell carcinoma and its associated venous involvement.
MRI is a noninvasive, safe and accurate method of diagnosing and staging of renal cell carcinoma with venacaval thrombi.
magnetic resonance imaging is an accurate method of assessing vena caval thrombosis.

MR imaging is a very good noninvasive method for evaluating the extent of tumor thrombus.
magnetic resonance imaging provides a reliable method for assessing the presence and extent vena caval tumor involvement and can obviate the need for invasive studies.
the use of magnetic resonance imaging for the evaluation of renal cell carcinoma is a useful and accurate diagnostic modality.

magnetic resonance imaging is the best study to determine the extent of the tumor thrombus.
